paper.title: No-Regret Learning in Bilateral Trade via Global Budget Balance

settings.name_in_paper: Repeated bilateral trade with global budget balance, full feedback
unmapped: Actions are pairs of prices (p,q) in [0,1]^2 posted to seller and buyer; reward is gain from trade 1{s_t<=p}1{q<=b_t}(b_t-s_t), discontinuous in prices
Global budget balance: cumulative profit sum_t 1{s_t<=p_t}1{q_t<=b_t}(q_t-p_t) must be non-negative almost surely; budget starts at 0 and is replenished by profits
Regret benchmark is best fixed budget-balanced price pair (p<=q) in hindsight
settings.definition_quote: At each time step t, a new pair of buyer and seller arrives, characterized by valuations b_t in [0,1] and s_t in [0,1]... We restrict the learner to enforce a global budget balance property which states that the final budget B_T has to be non-negative with probability 1. ... Full feedback: at the end of each round, the agents reveal their valuations (i.e. z_t = (s_t, b_t)).

settings.name_in_paper: Repeated bilateral trade with global budget balance, one-bit feedback
unmapped: Actions are price pairs (p,q) in [0,1]^2; reward is gain from trade
Feedback is only one bit: whether the trade happened, 1{s_t<=p_t}1{q_t<=b_t}; gain from trade is not observed
Global budget balance: cumulative profit must be non-negative almost surely
Benchmark: best fixed budget-balanced price in hindsight
settings.definition_quote: One-bit feedback: the learner only observes whether the trade happened or not (i.e. z_t = 1{s_t <= p_t} * 1{q_t <= b_t}).

settings.name_in_paper: Repeated bilateral trade with global budget balance, two-bit feedback (lower bound)
unmapped: Actions are price pairs (p,q) in [0,1]^2; reward is gain from trade
Global budget balance: cumulative profit must be non-negative almost surely
Benchmark: best fixed budget-balanced price in hindsight
settings.definition_quote: Two-bit feedback: the agents only reveal their willingness to accept the prices offered by the learner (i.e. z_t is composed by the two bits (1{s_t <= p_t}, 1{q_t <= b_t}))

algorithms.name: GFT-Max with Hedge (Profit-Max phase on F_K, then Hedge on H_K)
GFT-Max with EXP3.P (Profit-Max phase) and Block-Decomposition with GFT-Est (second phase)

conditions: learner must satisfy global budget balance almost surely
comparator: best fixed price pair (p,q) with p<=q in hindsight
tuning: Hedge as regret minimizer in both phases

source.label: thm:full_upper
source.quote: Consider the repeated bilateral trade problem in the full feedback model. There exists a learning algorithm $\cA$ that respects global budget balance and whose regret with respect to the best fixed price in hindsight verifies \[ R_T(\cA) \le 92 \,\log^{\nicefrac 3 2}(T)\,\sqrt{T }. \]

results.notes: Regret is max over fixed prices of realized GFT on the adversarial sequence minus expected GFT of the learner; worst case over sequences.

conditions: any learning algorithm that satisfies global budget balance

source.label: thm:full_lower
source.quote: Consider the repeated bilateral trade problem in the full feedback model. Any learning algorithm that satisfies global budget balance suffers at least $\Omega(\sqrt{T})$ regret with respect to the best fixed price in hindsight.

results.notes: Proof gives explicit 5*sqrt(T)/216 via Yao's principle with i.i.d. random valuations from three points; Lemma used requires T large enough.

conditions: learner must satisfy global budget balance almost surely
comparator: best fixed price pair (p,q) with p<=q in hindsight
tuning: EXP3.P on F_K in phase I
Block-Decomposition with Hedge and N = T^(1/2) blocks in phase II

source.label: thm:partial_upper
source.quote: Consider the repeated bilateral trade problem in the one-bit feedback model. There exists a learning algorithm $\cA$ that respects global budget balance and whose regret with respect to the best fixed price in hindsight verifies: \[ R_T(\cA) \le 1282\cdot T^{\nicefrac34}\log^2 T. \]

results.notes: Restatable theorem without printed annotation; number given by label. Also applies to two-bit feedback (more informative).

conditions: any learning algorithm that satisfies global budget balance

source.label: thm:lower2bits
source.quote: Consider the problem of repeated bilateral trade in the two-bit feedback model. Any learning algorithm that satisfies global budget balance suffers regret at least $\Omega(T^{\nicefrac57})$.

results.notes: Hard instances are i.i.d. stochastic valuation distributions; also implies the bound for one-bit feedback.

symbols.alpha_apx: multiplicative factor alpha in the alpha-regret

conditions: any globally budget balanced learning algorithm with full feedback
benchmark is the best fixed budget-feasible distribution over prices (budget balance in expectation)

source.label: thm:alpha_lower
source.quote: Fix any constant $\alpha \in [1,\nicefrac {36}{35})$, and any globally budget balanced learning algorithm $\cA$ with full-feedback. Then there exists a sequence of valuations such that \[ \sum_{t=1}^T \mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{(p,q)\sim\gamma^*}{\gft_t(p,q)} - \alpha \cdot \sum_{t=1}^T \E{\gft_t(p_t,q_t)} \ge \tfrac 5{18} \left(\tfrac{36}{35} - \alpha \right)T, \]

results.notes: Comparator is the best feasible distribution over prices (Definition 2.1), mapped to best_feasible_policy. Linear lower bound.

conditions: benchmark is the best fixed budget-feasible distribution over prices

source.label: cor:2-regret
source.quote: Let $\cA$ be a learning algorithm for the repeated bilateral trade problem which guarantees an upper bound of $f(T)$ on the regret with respect to the best fixed price in hindsight. Then, the $2$-regret of $\mathcal{A}$ with respect to the best budget feasible distribution over prices is at most $f(T)$.

results.notes: Corollary is generic in f(T); instantiated with f(T) from Theorem 4.2 (combining with Theorem 6.3).

conditions: benchmark is the best fixed budget-feasible distribution over prices

source.label: cor:2-regret
source.quote: Let $\cA$ be a learning algorithm for the repeated bilateral trade problem which guarantees an upper bound of $f(T)$ on the regret with respect to the best fixed price in hindsight. Then, the $2$-regret of $\mathcal{A}$ with respect to the best budget feasible distribution over prices is at most $f(T)$.

results.notes: Generic corollary instantiated with the one-bit bound of Theorem (thm:partial_upper).
